holidays.name: National Pound Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy dense, buttery, golden pound cake. Eat it plain, or dress it up with berries and whipped cream. Toasting a slice in a skillet with extra butter is a respectable choice too.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and nobody is sure who started it. The cake itself dates to 18th-century Europe. The original recipe was easy to remember: one pound each of butter, sugar, eggs and flour.
holidays.funFact: Early pound cakes had no baking powder or baking soda. Bakers got the rise by beating the eggs and butter for a long time, and that was hard work before electric mixers.

holidays.name: Toy Soldier Day
holidays.description: A salute to the tiny plastic, tin and lead figures that have fought many living-room battles. Collectors, hobbyists and nostalgic grown-ups can dust off a battalion and march it across the carpet.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a toy tradition that goes back centuries, with early flat tin figures made in Germany and mass-produced plastic armies following in the 20th century.
holidays.funFact: Author H.G. Wells, who wrote The War of the Worlds, also wrote a set of tabletop rules for toy soldier battles. They were published in 1913 as the book Little Wars.
